patch_description:
All prior programs plateau at min_area_normalized = 0.02. Two problems in the current code: (1) `_point_outside_hull` always returns True ("conservative"), and it's actually called incorrectly (indexes `cand` with an interior index but never receives the moved vertex index), so accepted moves get exact recomputes via a wrong path while rejected moves use approximate hull areas that may never update — the cached `hull_a` can go stale and corrupt the score silently. (2) The annealer only ever moves a single vertex at a time with adaptive sigma, which collapses to tiny local steps and cannot escape the incumbent basin — this is exactly why every program is stuck at 0.02.

Fix: (a) replace the acceptance block with an exact score recomputation on every accepted move (full 286-triangle numpy evaluation + monotone-chain hull is only microseconds, so correctness costs nothing while the incremental min-over-rest still screens candidates cheaply); (b) replace `_point_outside_hull` with a proper point-in-convex-polygon test; (c) add a basin-hopping mechanism: when no improvement for several rounds, kick 3-4 randomly chosen vertices simultaneously at sigma ~0.14 from the best-known configuration, then resume local annealing — coordinated multi-vertex kicks are far more likely to jump between basins than isotropic single-vertex noise, and the strict best-seen bookkeeping guarantees the returned result never regresses.
